summary:
Meridian Health Plan of New York sent a denial letter dated September 8, 2026. It denied coverage for an MRI of your left knee without contrast (CPT 73721) from Riverside Orthopedic Associates on August 20, 2026.

The plan says the service was not medically necessary. Its letter quotes guideline MHP-MSK-014 (Advanced Imaging of the Knee), which requires documentation of at least six weeks of conservative treatment. The denial code listed is 50.

The provider billed $2,400. Your plan paid $0. The letter does not state how much you may owe, and it does not state network status.

The letter says you or an authorized representative may file a written internal appeal within 180 days of receiving the notice.

terms.definition: A notice from your plan saying it will not cover a service, and why.
A plan's judgment about whether care was needed and appropriate.
The written medical rules or guidelines a plan uses to decide whether care is necessary.
Simpler, non-surgical care such as rest, medication, or physical therapy tried before advanced testing or procedures.
Your first appeal, decided by the plan itself.
A short code a plan uses on a notice to show the reason a claim or request was denied.
Whether a provider has a contract with your plan (in network) or not (out of network).
A person you allow to act for you in dealing with your plan, such as a family member or your doctor.
